subject: Genetics
title: X-Linked Inheritance
description: A quick win: understand X-Linked Inheritance.

hook.text: Hemophilia plagued European royals for generations. It passed through mothers and struck only sons.

buildup.text: X-linked diseases sit on the X chromosome. Males have one X, so one bad copy means disease. Females have a backup.

discovery.text: Queen Victoria carried hemophilia. Through her daughters, it spread to the Spanish, German, and Russian courts.

twist.text: Females can be affected too if they inherit two bad X copies—rare, but it happens.

climax.text: X-linked patterns explain why some diseases are almost exclusively male. The chromosome itself is the filter.

punchline.text: One X. No backup. Sons pay the price.

quiz.question: Why do X-linked diseases mostly affect males?
options: Males have only one X chromosome, so no backup copy
Males are exposed to more toxins
